news.headline: Buy low: Zubac, Boozer, Ajay Mitchell and Gobert
news.take: Good targets if a manager is fed up. Don’t overpay; the bounce-back may take weeks.
news.detail: Their efficiency and minutes have dipped, but the underlying roles look stable. The show expects Boozer to finish as a top 30–40 player and Zubac back in the top 80–95.

news.headline: Cade (knee) questionable; Reaves (heel) and Nembhard (hip) out
news.take: Check each status before the daily lock. If IR is full, bench players who are out rather than leaving them in the lineup.
news.detail: Cunningham sat Wednesday with a knee issue and is day-to-day. Reaves did a pregame workout that went well, but the Lakers have given no return date. Nembhard missed Wednesday with a hip problem.

news.headline: Deni Avdija (foot) questionable for Thursday
news.take: Start him if he is cleared before the Thursday lock (Friday about 8 AM MYT).
news.detail: Avdija missed Tuesday against Minnesota with a foot problem and is listed questionable against Milwaukee. He has been playing about 33 minutes a night when healthy.

news.headline: Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson are trending out of favor
news.take: Fair for deep benches. Hachimura still plays about 27 minutes, so he works as a short-term fill-in, not a long hold.
news.detail: Josh Lloyd says neither needs to be held in standard leagues: Hachimura is shooting poorly from the field and Jackson has lost minutes.

news.headline: Wendell Carter Jr., Jalen Smith and Coby White are must-roster players
news.take: Agree on the roles, but Carter has cooled over the last week. Hold, don’t chase at a premium.
news.detail: All three are still unowned in too many leagues according to the show. Carter brings rebounds and efficient shooting; Jalen Smith has a steady role; White adds scoring and threes.

news.headline: Sell Anthony Black before his minutes fade
news.take: His steals rate is unlikely to last. Sell if a fair offer comes.
news.detail: Black’s minutes, usage and steals have jumped while Orlando is short-handed. The show expects them to drop once the roster is healthy and suggests selling for any top-70 player.

news.headline: Sell high: Siakam, Norman Powell, Huerter and Saddiq Bey
news.take: Siakam and Powell are still useful starters, so only sell for clear value. Huerter and Bey are fine to move.
news.detail: Siakam’s usage should fall when Haliburton returns; Powell’s surge comes from injuries around him and hot two-point shooting; Huerter and Bey are riding unusual block and shooting numbers.
